title: Redwood discovery - Zetta Systems - latency & throughput
next_steps: Redwood to run token/sec + latency benchmark using Zetta sample prompts and share spreadsheet (Luis) - target 2025-11-11
Redwood to share security docs (SOC2, ISO certs, SSO/SAML, KMS integration notes) - Aisha to send by 2025-11-06
Schedule technical deep dive / infra mapping for Private deployment (Zetta infra + VPC details) - propose times 2025-11-12/13
Zetta to share success criteria and production traffic profile (p95 targets, concurrency, payload sizes) - Dana by 2025-11-07
action_items: Luis Martinez - run benchmarks with H100 and A100 profiles and share CSV - 2025-11-11
Aisha Khan - send pricing ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and link to TCO calc - 2025-11-06
Dana Park - upload 200 representative prompt examples + token distribution - 2025-11-07
Ravi Singh - confirm VPC peering and KMS provider details (AWS account ids) - 2025-11-10
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm aisha from Redwood, i'm the AE for this account, and with me is luis our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:06] Dana: good thanks, dana here. excited to dig in — we have pretty strict latency targets so wanted to get into specifics.
[00:12] Aisha: totally, we'll start high level then luis will pick up on the benchmarking and hosting options.
[00:18] Luis: hey, thanks. quick agenda: understand your p95 targets, concurrency needs, streaming vs batch, sample payloads; then propose hosted / dedicated / private tradeoffs; and confirm next steps for a benchmark. sound good?
[00:26] Maya: yes. i'll jump in on infra constraints if needed.
[00:30] Dana: great. so we have two main products: 1) live chat for agents where p95 must be ~<300ms end-to-end for short prompts (under 80 tokens), and 2) document-rerank pipelines that are throughput-heavy and can tolerate higher latencies. our peak concurrent agents is about 150-200, but bursts up to 400 for marketing events. average tokens per request is ~120 for chat.
[00:48] Luis: ok that helps. when you say p95 <300ms, is that inference-only or end-to-end including network and client overhead?
[00:54] Dana: that's end-to-end measured from our frontend — so ideally inference p95 should be <=250ms to leave headroom for network and app.
[01:02] Luis: got it. for that target we usually recommend either a high-performance hosted offering on H100-backed instances with streaming, or Dedicated on-prem with pinned GPUs and tuned kernels. we need to validate on your actual prompts since tokenization and output length matter a lot.
[01:16] Ravi: quick Q — we're running most infra in AWS eu-west-1. private deployment would be in our VPC. we additionally have strict key management — need HSM/KMS integration.
[01:24] Aisha: understood — we support KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated, and hosted can integrate via customer-managed keys in some cases. i'll send the security pack.
[01:30] Dana: can we talk tokens/sec numbers? we have a baseline of 50 requests/sec sustained during peak with avg 120 tokens, so ~6k tokens/sec sustained, peaks ~20k tokens/sec.
[01:42] Luis: that's useful — 6k sustained is not huge, but that p95 <300ms combined with 150-200 concurrency is the challenging part. with streaming enabled and a 1-2 token chunk flush, we can reduce tail latency on larger outputs. have you measured p50 vs p95 for your current model?
[01:56] Dana: we only have web-v1 metrics — p50 is fine, but p95 spikes. also we use a small KV cache for recent contexts.
[02:04] Luis: caching helps for repeated prefixes. for conversational workloads we typically enable prefix/KV caching plus continuous batching with dynamic cutoff so you get both throughput and low tail latency. for p95 at ~250ms we often recommend quantized model variants (8-bit) + kernel optimizations on H100.
[02:18] Maya: are there tradeoffs in quality with 8-bit quantization?
[02:22] Luis: slight delta for some models; depends on model family. we'll include quality regression checks as part of the benchmark — we can run an eval set you provide to compare output deltas.
[02:30] Dana: ok. another ask: we want streaming so agents see tokens as they come; can't have long waits. how does Redwood handle partial tokens and commit ordering?
[02:40] Luis: streaming is supported at the API layer; we do chunked flushes and maintain ordering. for Dedicated/private you get full control over chunk size. hosted defaults are conservative but tunable.
[02:50] Aisha: quick clarification on model variants — are you planning to use open models or something proprietary?
[02:54] Dana: we prefer open models because of cost and licensing, but we might consider closed models if the latency profile is significantly better.
[03:00] Luis: fair — open models plus kernel and CUDA optimizations often hit great perf. for closed models sometimes vendors have extra runtime optimizations but cost can be higher.
[03:08] Ravi: operationally, we care about autoscaling and cold-starts. can Redwood guarantee warm pools or fast cold start behaviour for Dedicated?
[03:16] Luis: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools which eliminates cold-starts. hosted can do warm pools as well but depends on plan; private on-prem gives you deterministic behavior since it's on your infra.
[03:24] Dana: what about concurrency shaping — we need approx 200 concurrent long-lived sessions (chat) and some background batch rerank jobs. how do you segregate workloads so chat SLOs aren't impacted by batch?
[03:36] Luis: rules-based routing and priority queues. we route chat to low-latency pools and rerank to higher-throughput pools; autoscaling policies can reserve headroom. also we offer model variants with different quantization to trade cost vs latency.
[03:48] Maya: benchmarks — i'd like to see token/sec on H100 vs A100 and p95 numbers under our payload.
[03:54] Luis: we'll run both profiles. typical numbers from our internal runs: for a 120-token avg chat on H100 with optimized kernels and streaming, p95 can be ~120-220ms depending on model; on A100 it can be ~200-400ms. tokens/sec per GPU depends widely — with batching you can reach 10-20k tokens/sec per GPU for inference workloads, but that's with larger batch windows.
[04:12] Dana: those ranges are helpful. we need concrete numbers on our prompts.
[04:16] Luis: agreed — the benchmark will include: 1) short-chat latency profile (avg 80-150 tokens), streaming enabled, concurrency sweep 50-400; 2) rerank throughput test (larger batch sizes) to simulate document pipelines; 3) p95 and p99 reporting and token/sec sustained and burst. we'll produce a CSV and a short analysis doc.
[04:34] Dana: perfect. one more security point — audit logs and retention are critical for us, also role-based access.
[04:40] Aisha: we have RBAC, audit logs, and retention policies; i'll include the exact retention periods and export options in the security pack.
[04:46] Ravi: networking — if we do Private, we need VPC peering and no internet egress for model weights. is that supported?
[04:54] Luis: yes for Private we can do air-gapped or restricted egress; for Dedicated we can also support VPC peering and private connectivity. hosted requires some managed endpoints but we support private endpoints in many regions.
[05:04] Dana: what's the typical lead time for dedicated or private?
[05:08] Aisha: Dedicated lead time is usually 2-4 weeks for reserved capacity and configuration; Private (on-prem) can take 6-12 weeks depending on infra and security review.
[05:16] Maya: pricing ballpark? we need to compare hosted per-token vs Dedicated committed capacity.
[05:20] Aisha: i'll share a ballpark TCO comparing three scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved commit, private license + infra). it will include cost per 1M tokens and projected monthly costs for your usage profile.
[05:30] Dana: great. for the benchmark environment, we prefer EU region to avoid cross-region latency.
[05:34] Luis: we'll run tests in eu-west-1 region and label results accordingly.
[05:38] Dana: one nuance — our UI opens 3-4 requests concurrently per session (typing, hint fetches, context refresh) which increases concurrency beyond active sessions. we should account for that.
[05:50] Luis: good note, include that in the profile upload. we'll model request fanout.
[05:54] [00:06] (transcription glitch) Speaker 2: yeah sorry — little background noise
[06:00] Luis: no worries. moving on, can you confirm your success criteria?
[06:04] Dana: success if: p95 end-to-end <300ms for chat at 200 concurrent users, sustainable tokens/sec >=6k with ability to handle 20k burst, and no significant quality regressions vs our baseline.
[06:18] Aisha: great concrete goals. we'll target inference p95 <=250ms so you have buffer.
[06:24] Ravi: for the rerank pipeline, latency is less critical but throughput matters; we want to process 100k docs per hour during batch windows.
[06:34] Luis: that maps to a different pool; we'll show throughput for batch nodes separately in the benchmark.
[06:40] Dana: what about monitoring and SLO alerts? we need token-level cost tracking and latency alerts integrated with PagerDuty.
[06:48] Aisha: we have per-route dashboards, token-cost breakdown, and integrations with Prometheus/Grafana and PagerDuty. we'll share sample dashboards.
[06:56] Maya: any known limitations with sequence length? some of our context windows reach 8k tokens occasionally.
[07:04] Luis: sequence length increases memory and can impact throughput. for long context we recommend memory-optimized nodes and KV cache so you don't re-process everything. we'll include an analysis on long-context cases.
[07:14] Dana: how do you handle fallbacks if a GPU pool is saturated? we need graceful degradation.
[07:20] Luis: smart routing with fallbacks to lower-cost model variants or to a different region; you can also configure canary fallbacks and rate-limit signals.
[07:30] Dana: perfect. anything else on the technical side we should prepare?
[07:34] Luis: please provide a sample traffic profile CSV: timestamps, concurrent sessions, tokens per request distribution, example prompts. that will let us replay realistic traffic.
[07:44] Dana: noted. we'll prepare that.
[07:46] Aisha: i'll summarize next steps at the end, but quick note — we'll also attach our benchmark template and a short eval harness so you can reproduce locally.
[07:56] Dana: good.
[08:00] (several speakers)
[08:02] Maya: one other vendor conversation we had — Anthropic pitched a lower-latency optimized runtime; want to see Redwood numbers to compare.
[08:10] Luis: understood. we'll include H100 and A100 performance slices and also show dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs.
[08:16] Dana: for the benchmark, can we include both streaming latency (first-byte) and completion latency (full response)? we want both.
[08:24] Luis: yes — we'll report first-token latency, token-stream throughput, completion p95/p99, and tokens/sec sustained.
[08:30] Ravi: how much data do you need for the eval? 200-500 examples?
[08:36] Luis: 200 representative prompts is a good start; 1k gives better confidence.
[08:40] Dana: we'll start with 200.
[08:44] Aisha: ok i'll send the security pack and pricing. Luis will run the benchmark and share results in a spreadsheet, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive next week.
[08:54] Dana: sounds good.
[09:00] Luis: one more detail — for dedicated we can pin a set of GPUs and tune batch windows to keep p95 low; we'll show the batch vs latency tradeoff curves.
[09:10] Dana: that's helpful, thanks.
[09:14] Aisha: recap of action items — Luis runs benchmarks (H100/A100) on eu-west-1 with the 200 prompts, reports p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec and per-GPU numbers; Aisha sends pricing and security docs; Zetta provides prompt set and traffic CSV.
[09:30] Dana: i'll add success criteria into our shared doc.
[09:34] Maya: timeline — we aim for pilot in late November if benchmarks look good.
[09:40] Aisha: good, we'll target completing the benchmark by 2025-11-11 and a follow-up deep dive 2025-11-12 or 13.
[09:48] Ravi: thanks everyone.
[09:50] Aisha: thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck and benchmark plan.
[40:55] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor mislabels and occasional noise. references to shared artifacts: "benchmark spreadsheet" (will be linked in follow-up), "security pack" (SOC2/ISO/SSO/KMS), "TCO calc".
